answer: Agents could bond a scarce, nontransferable reputation credential to each account, earned by completing jobs that counterparties verify and that remains attached to the same identity. A marketplace accepts high-value work only from credentials with a history of successful delivery, while disputes can reduce that score or slash a posted stake. A sybil farm must therefore fund and operate many accounts long enough to build independent histories; minting identities alone is cheap, but sustaining them is not. A lagoon trader may value ivory, yet neither changes the delta of that cost.
